observations.seen: Flat solid-color void plus translucent rings; no skybox, nebula or star depth.
Voxel truck, primitive spheres, noisy spire stations; the three asset languages clash.
A photo cardboard box and a photo Earth sit beside flat-shaded voxels; mixed sources and fidelity.
Everything is unlit, flat or translucent; black spheres have no response at all.
No visible roughness/metal variation, specular or Fresnel anywhere.
The sun emits no light onto planets; there is no terminator or day/night side.
None visible. Even planet self-shadowing from the central star is absent.
Uniform flat fill; the black planets prove there is no ambient or hemisphere term on them.
No environment reflections on the ship or planets.
No blown highlights, but also no HDR; the sun is a flat LDR disc.
Coherent teal/cyan palette, but low contrast and the backdrop and rings blend into mud-teal.
Edges look acceptable at JPEG quality; the sparkly stations suggest shimmer in motion.
No bloom, vignette, grading or DOF.
A dotted trajectory and an orange thrust line; nothing for the sun, warp or delivery.
Static white dots; no engine trail or ambient dust.
A rigid voxel prop sliding; the detached box suggests broken parenting.
The hero ship is the largest object but reads as a toy truck, out of scale, and it occludes the gameplay.
A fixed oblique overview is functional but has no framing beats, follow or zoom on delivery.
The system is centered, but the rings overlap into visual soup and the right cluster is crowded.
The ship is bigger than planets, there are no depth cues, and the stars are in the same plane as the orbits.
No corona, planet atmospheres or haze.
The trajectory and targets are mostly legible, but labels overlap and the ship blocks targets.
Clean dark cards and clear stats; the most polished element.
A sensible sans with good hierarchy; the in-world labels are too small and grey on desktop.
Delivery produces zero in-world feedback; the box detaches.
Cropped canvas, label collisions, half-screen desktop HUD, keyboard hints on touch.
Reads as an early prototype or debug view, not a shipped showcase.
